items.title: CVE-2026-129453 — A vulnerability was found in DrayTek Vigor2960 1.5.1.6. This issue affects the function ch…
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-129453 (score CVSS 9.9).

A vulnerability was found in DrayTek Vigor2960 1.5.1.6. This issue affects the function check_file_exist of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi of the component File Existence Check. Performing a manipulation of the argument upload_name results in heap-based buffer overflow. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is capable of addressing this issue.
items.detail:

Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is capable of addressing this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

items.title: CVE-2026-129483 — Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SRP serve…
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-129483 (score CVSS 9.1).

Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values A that are multiples of N. Unauthenticated network clients can send A equal to N to force a zero shared secret, authenticating as any existing user without the password and learning session keys.

items.title: Meta Fined €805 Million in Italy Over Facebook’s Default Photo Gallery Access
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique affectant Android.

Italy fines Meta €805 million over Facebook’s access to Android users’ photo galleries without specific consent, affecting around 20 million people. Italy’s data protection authority, the Garante, has fined Meta Platforms Ireland Limited €805 million.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique affectant Android.

Italy fines Meta €805 million over Facebook’s access to Android users’ photo galleries without specific consent, affecting around 20 million people. Italy’s data protection authority, the Garante, has fined Meta Platforms Ireland Limited €805 million. The reason is that the Facebook app for Android reached into photos, videos, and their metadata on Italian users’ phones without specific consent and without telling people properly what was happening. “The Italian Data Protection Authority (Garante) has fined Meta Platforms Ireland Limited €805 million. Through the Facebook app for Android devices, the company accessed photos, videos, and related metadata stored on Italian users’ smartphones without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them.” reads the Garante’s announcement . “The measure concerns the ‘Get tips from your gallery while browsing Facebook’ feature, available since 2023, which, while browsing, shows users photos and videos from their phone gallery as suggestions to post.” The feature at the center of the case suggests photos and videos from users’ phone gallery as things to post while they scroll Facebook. items.title: Data Breach at La Poste Subsidiary Maileva Affects 22 Million People in France
items.body:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Security Affairs.

A cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary Maileva exposed the names and postal addresses of 22 million people, including patients and tenants. Maileva, a subsidiary of the La Poste group, was hit in mid-September in one of the biggest cyberattacks France has seen. La Poste confirmed it to AFP..
items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Security Affairs.

A cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary Maileva exposed the names and postal addresses of 22 million people, including patients and tenants. Maileva, a subsidiary of the La Poste group, was hit in mid-September in one of the biggest cyberattacks France has seen. La Poste confirmed it to AFP.. The stolen data includes first names, last names and postal addresses of 22 million people, which are “recipients of Maileva’s client companies .” The company confirms bank details weren’t compromiseda. The specialized sites FrenchBreaches and Cyberattaque.org had flagged the breach first. According to Le Monde , Maileva sends documents on behalf of companies, including payslips, registered letters, invoices and shareholder meeting notices. It is part of Docaposte, a subsidiary of La Poste, and says it serves more than 70,000 users. In 2024, it sent 180 million documents. However, the 22 million people affected by the breach are not Maileva’s customers. They are the people who received documents sent through its platform. This is important because most of these people had never heard of Maileva and had no direct relationship with the company. According to Cyberattaque.org, the affected organizations include social housing providers such as Flandre Opale Habitat and Altéal, as well as medical laboratories belonging to the Inovie group, including AXBIO, BioMedilab and Bi

items.title: The Microsoft Outage Left 15 Hotel Guests Poisoned by Chlorine
items.body:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Security Affairs.

A Microsoft 365 outage stopped a hotel’s email chlorine alert in Germany, and 15 guests were poisoned. A hotel in Germany had a maintenance safety system for its sauna area. If the chlorine level got too high, the system emailed the operators. When Microsoft’s cloud services failed, those emails couldn’t go out, the chlorine rose, and 15 guests were poisoned, according to Notebookcheck report .

When Microsoft’s cloud services failed, those emails couldn’t go out, the chlorine rose, and 15 guests were poisoned, according to Notebookcheck report . “Over a dozen guests at a theme park hotel in Germany were injured by excessive chlorine levels.” states Notebookcheck . “According to local media reports, the incident was caused by a problem with the email-based system used to control chlorine dosing, which was affected by the Microsoft outage.” German emergency services sent 40 first responders. Local media reported that four victims were taken to hospital, and one stayed for further observation. items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Cyberattaque.org.

CodinGame, la plateforme française de programmation utilisée par des développeurs du monde entier, confirme avoir été victime d'une cyberattaque dans la

Attaque Mis à jour le 15 novembre 2026 à 12h15 CodinGame victime d’une cyberattaque : des messages privés exposés CodinGame, la plateforme française de programmation utilisée par des développeurs du monde entier, confirme avoir été victime d’une cyberattaque dans la nuit du 7 au 8 novembre 2026. Un individu non autorisé a exploité une vulnérabilité dans un outil interne pour copier des données issues de plusieurs bases informatiques. L’entreprise considère que l’ensemble des comptes utilisateurs est potentiellement concerné. Parmi les informations exposées figurent des adresses email, des identifiants de connexion, des adresses IP et, pour certains membres, des messages privés.

Créée en 2012 à Montpellier, CodinGame est une plateforme spécialisée dans l’apprentissage de la programmation à travers des jeux, des défis et des compétitions informatiques. Elle permet aux développeurs de tester leurs compétences dans différents langages et de participer à des challenges, parfois organisés avec des entreprises qui recrutent. Rachetée en 2021 par l’entreprise américaine CoderPad, elle appartient aujourd’hui à un groupe spécialisé dans l’évaluation des compétences techniques et le recrutement de développeurs.

Dans une notification dont Cyberattaque.org s’est procuré une copie, CodinGame détaille les circonstances de l’intrusion.

Kurz vor dem Black Friday zeigt eine neue Studie: 43 Prozent der Verbraucher haben eine E-Mail gelöscht oder ignoriert, weil sie an ihrer Echtheit zweifelten. Mehr als die Hälfte bevorzugt Marken mit verifiziertem Logo im Posteingang. DigiCert hat die Ergebnisse einer globalen Verbraucherstudie veröffentlicht. Sie zeigt: Die Angst vor gefälschten E-Mails kostet Händler die Aufmerksamkeit ihrer Kunden und möglicherweise auch deren Geschäft. Den Daten zufolge haben 43 Prozent der Verbraucher im vergangenen Jahr eine E-Mail gelöscht oder nicht weiter beachtet, weil sie sich ihrer Echtheit nicht sicher waren. 17 Prozent verschoben einen Kauf, mehr als jeder Zehnte kaufte bei einem anderen Händler. Die Ergebnisse verweisen auf eine Herausforderung kurz vor dem Black Friday: Nur 3 Prozent der Käufer würden ein Angebot öffnen oder anklicken, wenn sie nicht überprüfen können, ob es tatsächlich von der Marke stammt. Mehr als die Hälfte würde es löschen, ignorieren oder melden. „Käufer sollten nicht jedes Mal Detektiv spielen müssen, wenn ein Angebot in ihrem Posteingang landet", sagt Al Iverson, Industry Research and Community Engagement Lead bei Valimail, einem Unternehmen von DigiCert. „Händler können dabei helfen, indem sie ihre E-Mails schwerer fälschbar und leichter erkennbar machen. items.detail:
Signal de veille — Hacker News.

The ridesharing giant said drivers' license information stored by AI cloud company Fireworks AI was stolen during a security incident.

Uber confirms hackers stole thousands of drivers’ license information in data breach Zack Whittaker 6:57 AM PST · November 13, 2026 Uber is notifying thousands of drivers that their personal and driver’s license information was stolen during an October data breach at one of the company’s tech providers.

In notices filed this week with several U.S. attorneys general, including California , the ride-hail giant said it was notified on October 9 by the provider that hackers broke in and stole internal credentials, which were used to access Uber’s data.

The company said it subsequently began notifying affected drivers that their personal information was stored with the provider.

TechCrunch has learned that the provider is Fireworks AI, which lets developers access and use open AI models. Fireworks reported a data breach last month in which hackers stole its customers’ information, including billing data and some private AI datasets.

Online productivity startup Notion confirmed its data was also stolen in the Fireworks hack.

“The notices to drivers are in relation to a security incident impacting one of our third-party vendors, Fireworks.ai, which had access to some Uber data,” an Uber spokesperson told TechCrunch, deferring our questions to Fireworks.
